results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

results.draft_locus: whole draft
results.finding: All 16 aligned units' summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p16). The three opening callouts are house-format blocks, not spec paragraphs, and are matched to null; they restate the thesis and add no off-spec idea. The part lead paragraphs p06, p07, p10 and p11 do not restate their confused pairs, but their core idea (the part's terms in one table, each linked to its owning chapter) matches, and the pairs are named in KEY POINTS bullet 1 and explained by p03's slash-row sentence.

results.draft_locus: How to Use This Glossary ¶2
results.finding: The outliner marked only this unit as two ideas (how a table works / Veldmark is fictional). The spec's controlling idea for p03 includes 'Veldmark rows are fiction' as part of how to read a row, and the Veldmark sentence tells the reader how to read the rows that name Veldmark, so the unit serves one idea: how to read a section and its rows. No other unit was marked.

results.draft_locus: whole draft
results.finding: Every unit ties to a supporting claim: p01 to G1/G2 (the contact/conversation/lead example and the one-definition, one-owner rule); p02-p04 and the Veldmark and index units to G3 (the lookup layout); the part lead paragraphs to G2/G3 (owning chapters, neighbors in one table); p15 to G2; p16 points to the sources behind the definitions (G2).

results.draft_locus: whole draft
results.finding: The hook example is explained in p01 ('a report that adds the three together counts nothing useful'). Every definition table is explained by p03 (what a row is, that the last column gives the full treatment, that slash rows define confusable terms together) and by its lead paragraph naming the owning chapters; the Veldmark table is explained by p13 as fiction collected because the names recur.

results.draft_locus: whole draft
results.finding: Each boundary expresses its declared relationship and picks up the declared known information: s-how elaboration ('The sections follow the book's structure'), p03 elaboration ('Each section opens with...'), s-reading sequence ('The first section of definitions...'), Part I sequence ('From the book's own labels the page turns to its subject'), Part II elaboration ('Inside that business sits the thing being sold'), Part III sequence ('Once a listing is modeled, it has to arrive'), Part IV sequence ('Searchable inventory then has to meet buyers'), Part V cause_effect ('Matching strangers also draws fraud... so'), Part VI sequence ('A safe contact... is also where the money starts'), Part VII place ('Every part so far runs on one distributed system... underneath'), Part VIII sequence ('Above the platform sits the last part's vocabulary'), Veldmark contrast ('The terms so far describe real marketplace practice; this last section is different'), index conclusion_summary ('every row term... defined above, in one A–Z list'), p15 conclusion_summary ('Read together, the sections and this index'), p16 additional_support; the hand-off links [[bibliography]].

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶1 / How to Use This Glossary ¶1
results.quote: The section below explains how the page is laid out: a section of reading vocabulary, one section per part of the book, the Veldmark names and an alphabetical index at the end.
results.finding: Both flow readers read the layout twice: p01 ends by listing the sections, and p02 opens 'The sections follow the book's structure' and lists them again, which read as repetition rather than progress (A2: 'felt like déjà vu rather than progress'). The spec places a roadmap at the end of p01 and the full map in p02, and AC-2 needs the opening to predict the sections, so the overlap is partly built into the spec; the draft could make p02 announce itself as the detail of the layout just named instead of restating it.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 item B1 ('The next section then says almost the same thing ... so I read the layout twice')

results.draft_locus: Part III — Supply ¶1
results.quote: [[professional-seller-tooling]] owns what professionals use, including the lead ledger and lead management, the professional's side of the lead that Part VI defines.
results.finding: Both flow readers re-read this sentence: it sends them three sections ahead for 'lead', and the lead rows sit oddly under a section framed only as 'how inventory gets in and becomes searchable'. The spec's section idea includes professional tooling in Part III's scope, but the draft's framing sentence omits it, so the lead-ledger and lead-management rows look misplaced and split the contact/conversation/lead trio that KEY POINTS promised side by side.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-A, section 3 item A5 ('This tells me "lead" is only defined three sections later ... Instead they sit in two different sections')

results.draft_locus: Part VIII — Leadership table, Stressor analysis row
results.quote: Stressor / residue / attractor
results.finding: The Stressor analysis row uses 'the attractor' and 'the residue' one row before the 'Stressor / residue / attractor' row defines them; both flow readers read ahead and came back. Swapping the two rows fixes it.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 item B20 ('"Stressor / residue / attractor" is defined only in the next row, so I read the analysis row twice')

results.draft_locus: Introduction callouts and ¶1
results.finding: The intro reader predicted the expected organization (layout note, reading vocabulary, one section per part, Veldmark names, alphabetical index) and use (look a term up, read its neighbors, follow the link to the owning chapter), the one-meaning rule with disagreement needing correction, and the 2026 dating with a check of the current source before formal use. It noted only that the layout is announced and then repeated (see the flow results).

results.draft_locus: Part II and Part VI tables
results.finding: The cold reader stated the contact / conversation / lead difference (any reaching action; the platform-held thread about one listing; a rule-created record delivered to a professional and tracked to an outcome) owned by messaging-and-leads, and publication state (owned by the listing) versus enforcement overlay (owned by trust and safety), with visibility and contactability derived from both, owned by listing-aggregate — matching the expected answer.

results.draft_locus: Alphabetical Index ¶1 / Part V — Trust table
results.finding: The cold reader found ATO through the index under A, linked to Part V — Trust, read it as account takeover with the expected definition, and named fraud-prevention and identity-and-verification as owners — matching the expected answer. Minor friction it reported: the link lands on the section, not the row, and the row lists two chapters while the page promises one owning chapter.
